problem: The function $P(t)=710\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+{e}^{t})$ represents the volume of milk, in liters, produced on a farm $t$ days after the owner bought new cows. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the volume of produced milk as a function of $t?$

feedback.problem:
The inventory level $I,$ in hundreds of units, of a medical supply $t$ weeks after ordering begins, is modeled by

$$
I(t)={t}^{2}{e}^{-t}+12,\,t\ge 0.
$$

What is the instantaneous rate of change of the inventory level as a function of $t?$ 

The instantaneous rate of change of the inventory level is
{{field-1}} hundreds of units per week.
feedback.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the inventory level is ${I}^{′}(t).$

We take the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}^{′}(t) & =\frac{d}{dt}[{t}^{2}{e}^{-t}+12] \\  & =2t{e}^{-t}+{t}^{2}\cdot (-{e}^{-t}) \\  & =2t{e}^{-t}-{t}^{2}{e}^{-t} \\  & =t{e}^{-t}(2-t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change of the inventory level is $t{e}^{-t}(2-t)$ hundreds of units per week.
